liblzma: Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to reinit after LZ init failure

If the LZ-specific initialization (lz_init()) fails, the coder state may
be kept and reinitialized later. Forget the recorded dictionary size on
this error path so that a later reinitialization reallocates the
dictionary buffer instead of reusing a possibly stale one.

Reported-by: Maintainer I
(cherry picked from commit fe4d763d566a38ad61d4c5022520c25578a3a464)

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the entire filter chain should be cleaned up
with lzma_next_end(). lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init()
have always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.
(Separate cleanup is weird, but it must have made sense to the young me.)

The following decoders initialize LZMA1 filter directly without using the
raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all other filters
when a program is linked against static liblzma. These functions didn't
call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error, which left the state
available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_alone_decoder()
  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_auto_decoder() [*]

[*] lzma_auto_decoder() is only indirectly affected due to the first two
    functions. lzma_auto_decoder() itself doesn't need a fix.

There are also encoder functions that initialize the LZMA1 encoder
directly. They don't have this issue because the whole lzma_stream
is cleaned up when encoder initialization fails.

Reported-by: Maintainer I
(cherry picked from commit e5e63d50eac1b4357a5a7a0abd3c5f99a5c47881)

coupling:
Target defect: a use-after-free / NULL-pointer dereference in the LZMA dictionary reuse path, reached through the public lzma_microlzma_decoder() API by reinitializing one lzma_stream with a small, then a large, then a small dictionary while a custom lzma_allocator (in-contract public API) fails the large dictionary allocation. lzma_microlzma_decoder() reuses its inner LZMA/LZ decoder across reinitializations. In lzma_lz_decoder_init() a dictionary enlargement frees coder->dict.buf and tries to allocate a bigger buffer; on failure it returns LZMA_MEM_ERROR leaving coder->dict.buf == NULL but coder->dict.size still equal to the previous alloc_size. A later reinit back to the original size finds coder->dict.size == alloc_size, skips reallocation, and lz_decoder_reset() writes through the stale/NULL buffer (crash at lz_decoder.c:58).

The bug is delocalized across the two edited commits, each of which closes one of two INDEPENDENT safety layers:
  (A) commit 1d4774e (lz_decoder.c) originally reset coder->dict.size = 0 on the dictionary (re)allocation-failure path, guaranteeing a later reinit reallocates. My edit relocates that reset to the lz_init() failure branch -- a path that is NOT taken in this scenario -- so the dict-alloc-failure path no longer invalidates dict.size.
  (B) commit 4b3dbbc (microlzma_decoder.c) originally called lzma_next_end() when the LZMA filter init failed, discarding the inner coder so no stale state survives. My edit drops the microlzma case (keeping alone_decoder and lzip_decoder), so microlzma keeps the stale inner coder after the error.

Why a correct fix is non-local / fixing a single commit's diff leaves it reachable: layers (A) and (B) are redundant guards on the SAME reuse path, and each edited diff is self-consistent, correct-looking maintenance on its own -- (A) adds a reinit-safety reset on an alloc-failure path; (B) cleans up the decoders it enumerates. With only edit (A) applied, microlzma still calls lzma_next_end() on error (B intact) and the stale coder is torn down -> no bug (verified rc=0). With only edit (B) applied, lz_decoder_init() still resets dict.size=0 on dict-alloc failure (A intact) and the reinit reallocates -> no bug (verified rc=0). The crash appears ONLY when both edits are present, because exposing it requires that NEITHER the dictionary allocation-failure path invalidate dict.size (reasoning about lz_decoder.c) NOR microlzma discard its inner coder on error (reasoning about microlzma_decoder.c). No single diff contains an identifiable defect; a reviewer must reason jointly about lz_decoder_init()'s cross-call reuse semantics and microlzma_decode()'s error handling. Base (main) lacks both original fixes and already crashes on the PoC (regime=incomplete_fix); the unedited maint-batch has both fixes and is secure; the resulting tree crashes under ASan (rc 134).
